title: Geo silo verifier and certification witness for dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity require cryptographically verifiable, per-tenant residency and isolation statements (who processed the requests, where the compute ran, and how long data was retained). Current ad-hoc exports and manual attestations are slow, error-prone, and don't meet enterprise audit needs. Goal: Build an automated pipeline that emits a signed, tamper-evident "silo snapshot" for each dedicated tenant on a configurable cadence, with retention metadata and a verification API and console surface. The pipeline must integrate with KMS/HSM for signing, support configurable retention windows, produce human- and machine-readable artifacts, and be efficient (avoid scanning entire node disks every run). Success metrics: 1) Can generate and serve a signed snapshot for 95% of dedicated tenants within their SLA window (<= 15 minutes after snapshot time); 2) Reduces manual evidence requests to zero for routine residency audits; 3) Increases audit automation coverage to 90% of tenant requests in the first quarter after launch. Constraints & trade-offs: - Proof size vs frequency: high-frequency small deltas vs periodic full snapshots; we'll implement incremental snapshot diffs with periodic full baseline to balance cost. - Signer trust model: customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-signing; initial rollout supports Redwood KMS with an extension point for customer KMS later. - Verification latency: on-demand verification must be fast (<=500ms) so it can be embedded in compliance dashboards. - Storage cost: keep signed bundles in cold storage after 90 days and expose short-lived public verification receipts. - Legal/forensic: snapshots must include checksum of retained artifacts and pointer to audit logs, not raw tenant data. Implementation outline: 1) Snapshotter service (agent) runs on dedicated nodes to collect provenance metadata (node id, region, container images, kernel version, timestamped connection matrix) and retention markers. 2) Orchestrator collects agent outputs, composes a canonical JSON snapshot + manifest (checksums), and computes incremental diffs. 3) Signer service signs the manifest using KMS/HSM and stores signed bundles in encrypted blobstore with retention metadata. 4) Verification API verifies signature, returns structured proof, and emits human-readable attestations for regulatory requests. 5) Console surface and export: per-tenant proof timeline, export to PDF/ZIP, and scheduled evidence delivery (SFTP/Cloud Storage).
acceptance_criteria: Signed snapshot generation pipeline produces a manifest and signature for a sample dedicated tenant within 15 minutes of snapshot window end
Verification API validates signatures against the KMS public key and returns canonical proof within 500ms for 95% of requests
Snapshot manifests include tenant id, node ids, region tags, retention window, checksum list and pointer to audit logs
Retention lifecycle enforces deletion and transition policies documented in runbook (90d warm -> 365d cold -> deletion) and can be overridden per-tenant
Console displays per-tenant proof timeline and allows downloadable signed bundle (ZIP) with embedded verification metadata
End-to-end tests and a staging PRD demo completed and linked in ticket
